title: "03_arima"
format: html

```{r}
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
```


```{r}
crash_ts <- read.csv("../data/nyc_daily_crashes.csv") |>
  mutate(day = as.Date(day)) |>       # text back to date
  as_tsibble(index = day)             # back to a time series
```


```{r}
crash_ts |> 
autoplot(crash_ts)
```

```{r}
# pre-2020 describes a different regime than post-2020
train <-  crash_ts |> filter_index("2021-01-01" ~ "2024-12-31")
test <- crash_ts |> filter_index("2025-01-01" ~ "2025-12-31")

train |> 
  gg_tsdisplay(crashes, plot_type = "partial", lag_max = 35)
```
```{r}
train |>
  autoplot(crashes) +
  labs(title = "NYC Daily Crashes, Training Period (2021–2024)",
       y = "Crashes per day", x = NULL)
```


```{r}
# transformation check
train |> features(crashes, features = guerrero)

# how many seasonal (weekly) differences are needed?
train |> features(crashes, unitroot_nsdiffs, .period = 7)

# how many regular differences are needed?
train |> features(crashes, unitroot_ndiffs)

# alternative chec
train |> features(crashes, unitroot_kpss)
```

```{r}
train |>
  gg_tsdisplay(difference(crashes), plot_type = "partial", lag_max = 35)
```

```{r}
train |> 
  gg_tsdisplay(difference(crashes, 7), plot_type = "partial", lag_max = 35)
```

```{r}
train |> features(difference(crashes, 7), unitroot_kpss)
train |> features(difference(crashes, 7), unitroot_ndiffs)
```

The raw training series failed the KPSS test (statistic 6.86, p < 0.01). After a weekly seasonal difference, the series passed (statistic 0.047, p > 0.10), so the manual model uses D = 1 and d = 0.


```{r}
# fit manual and auto-selected ARIMA on the training data
fit <- train |>
  model(
    manual = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(1, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)),
    auto   = ARIMA(crashes)
  )

fit |> select(manual) |> report()
fit |> select(auto) |> report()
```

```{r}
# residual diagnostics for each model
fit |> select(manual) |> gg_tsresiduals(lag_max = 35)
fit |> select(auto)   |> gg_tsresiduals(lag_max = 35)

# Ljung-Box test: lag = 2 x seasonal period (14); dof = number of estimated coefficients
augment(fit) |> filter(.model == "manual") |> features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 14, dof = 2)
augment(fit) |> filter(.model == "auto")   |> features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 14, dof = 4)
```


```{r}
# forecast the 2025 test period
fc <- fit |> forecast(new_data = test)

# accuracy on the test set
accuracy(fc, crash_ts)

# forecast plots (Discussion 3 asks for both models)
fc |>
  filter(.model == "manual") |>
  autoplot(crash_ts |> filter_index("2024-07-01" ~ "2025-12-31")) +
  labs(title = "Manual ARIMA(1,0,0)(0,1,1)[7]: 2025 forecast", y = "Crashes per day", x = NULL)

fc |>
  filter(.model == "auto") |>
  autoplot(crash_ts |> filter_index("2024-07-01" ~ "2025-12-31")) +
  labs(title = "Auto ARIMA(0,1,2)(0,0,2)[7]: 2025 forecast", y = "Crashes per day", x = NULL)
```

```{r}
fit |> select(manual) |> gg_tsresiduals(lag_max = 35)

augment(fit) |> filter(.model == "manual") |>
  features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 14, dof = 2)
```

```{r}
# compare nearby manual models (same differencing, so AICc is comparable)
fit_try <- train |>
  model(
    m100 = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(1, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)),
    m101 = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(1, 0, 1) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)),
    m200 = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(2, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)),
    m201 = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(2, 0, 1) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7))
  )

glance(fit_try) |> arrange(AICc) |> select(.model, sigma2, AICc)
```

```{r}
# does a third AR term help?
fit_try3 <- train |>
  model(m300 = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(3, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)))
glance(fit_try3) |> select(.model, sigma2, AICc)

# residuals for m200
fit_try |> select(m200) |> gg_tsresiduals(lag_max = 35)

```
```{r}
# fit final manual model and auto model
fit <- train |>
  model(
    manual = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(2, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)),
    auto   = ARIMA(crashes)
  )

# forecast the 2025 test period and score it
fc <- fit |> forecast(new_data = test)
accuracy(fc, crash_ts) |> select(.model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE)
```

```{r}
fit <- train |>
  model(
    snaive = SNAIVE(crashes ~ lag("week")),
    manual = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(2, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7)),
    auto   = ARIMA(crashes)
  )
```

```{r}
# forecast the 2025 test period
fc <- fit |> forecast(new_data = test)

# accuracy on the test set
accuracy(fc, crash_ts) |> select(.model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE)

# manual model forecast plot
fc |>
  filter(.model == "manual") |>
  autoplot(crash_ts |> filter_index("2024-07-01" ~ "2025-12-31")) +
  labs(title = "Manual ARIMA(2,0,0)(0,1,1)[7]: 2025 Forecast",
       y = "Crashes per day", x = NULL)

# auto model forecast plot
fc |>
  filter(.model == "auto") |>
  autoplot(crash_ts |> filter_index("2024-07-01" ~ "2025-12-31")) +
  labs(title = "Auto ARIMA(0,1,2)(0,0,2)[7]: 2025 Forecast",
       y = "Crashes per day", x = NULL)
```

```{r}
# rolling-origin CV: start with 2 years of training, add 30 days each fold
train_cv <- train |>
  stretch_tsibble(.init = 730, .step = 30) |>
  relocate(day, .id)

# refit the manual model on every fold and forecast one week (one season) ahead
fc_cv <- train_cv |>
  model(manual = ARIMA(crashes ~ pdq(2, 0, 0) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 7))) |>
  forecast(h = 7) |>
  group_by(.id) |>
  mutate(h = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  as_fable(response = "crashes", distribution = crashes)

# overall CV accuracy
fc_cv |> accuracy(crash_ts) |> select(.model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE)

# accuracy by forecast horizon (1 to 7 days ahead)
fc_cv |>
  accuracy(crash_ts, by = c("h", ".model")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = h, y = MAE)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Cross-validated MAE by forecast horizon",
       x = "Days ahead", y = "MAE (crashes per day)")

# accuracy by fold: how the model holds up across time periods
fc_cv |>
  accuracy(crash_ts, by = c(".id", ".model")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .id, y = MAE)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Cross-validated MAE across rolling folds",
       x = "Fold (each adds 30 days of training data)", y = "MAE (crashes per day)")
```
